full_judgment:
2. This present petitioner as preemptor filed two preemption cases being Miscellaneous Case Nos.15 of 1996 and 16 of 1996 against the present respondent No.1 Md. Hazrat Ali and another under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur. His case was that he was a co-sharer of the case holding while the purchaser O.P. No.1 was a stranger to that. That the O.P. No.2 sold the case land to the O.P. No.1 by two registered kabalas dated 02.03.1996 beyond the knowledge of this petitioner. That knowing about those kabalas the petitioner filed the preemption cases within the statutory period of limitation after depositing the requisite amount. 

 7. Mr. Abdus Salam Khan, the learned senior advocate for the review petitioner has made submission to the effect that the purchaser O.P. was not a co-sharer of the case holding by virtue of inheritance and as such the pre-emption case against him was well maintainable. But we cannot accept this argument of the learned advocate for the petitioner in view of clause (a) of sub-section 10 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which was in force at the time of filing of the pre-emption case in question. This clause (a) of sub-section 10 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act clearly provided that pre-emption case was not maintainable in respect of a transfer to a co-sharer whose interest in the case holding accrued otherwise than by purchase. In this case the purchaser O.P. admittedly, acquired interest in the case holding by virtue of a registered deed of gift long before the case transfer. So, the pre-emption cases were not maintainable against him.
